subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: After real behavior proof is supplied, should repeated exec calls with the same arguments, nonzero exit code, and stable termination metadata count as no progress even when their output changes?
rationale: The patch correctly fixes the reported runaway loop, but this equivalence policy can also terminate retries whose only observable progress is changing error output; repository history and tests cannot determine the intended availability tradeoff.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero equivalence
options.body: Treat changing output from otherwise identical nonzero outcomes as no progress and land after exact-head live proof confirms the intended breaker behavior.

options.title: Limit stable hashing to hard failures
options.body: Keep ordinary nonzero completed outcomes output-sensitive, accepting that the common exit-code-1 path in the linked issue remains unfixed.

options.title: Pause the heuristic change
options.body: Do not merge until a more granular progress signal can distinguish meaningful nonzero retry progress from volatile failure noise.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero equivalence
recommendation.body: Treat changing output from otherwise identical nonzero outcomes as no progress and land after exact-head live proof confirms the intended breaker behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned reviewer identified the key runtime-contract issue and has recent merged history in both affected exec and loop-detection paths.
